answer.short:
$1^3+2^3+\cdots+n^3=T_n^2=\left(\frac{n(n+1)}2\right)^2$.

Add the identities from part (a); the intermediate triangular-number squares cancel.
answer.worked:
Substituting the requested values gives
$$\begin{align*}T_2^2-T_1^2&=2^3\\T_3^2-T_2^2&=3^3\\&\vdots\\T_n^2-T_{n-1}^2&=n^3.\end{align*}$$
Adding cancels the intermediate terms:
$$\begin{align*}2^3+3^3+\cdots+n^3&=(T_2^2-T_1^2)+(T_3^2-T_2^2)+\cdots+(T_n^2-T_{n-1}^2)\\2^3+3^3+\cdots+n^3&=T_n^2-T_1^2\\2^3+3^3+\cdots+n^3&=T_n^2-1.\end{align*}$$
Since $1^3=1$, adding 1 gives
$$1^3+2^3+3^3+\cdots+n^3=T_n^2.$$
